samples.summary: Select-all unset walks and buffers every styled cell in the sheet, then writes them all inside one batch — a collaborator-visible resource-exhaustion path
samples.evidence: In `unsetRangeStyleValues` the new pre-scan (packages/sheets/src/model/worksheet/sheet.ts:4292-4317) iterates `store.getGrid(range)` for every selected range, issues one `store.get(anchor)` per cell, and accumulates an unbounded `cellEdits` array in memory; the write phase (4373-4380) then performs one `store.set`/`store.delete` per buffered cell inside a single `beginBatch()/endBatch()` (4319/4382). With `selectAllCells()` the target range spans the used bounds, so a single 'Decrease decimal places' click on a large shared document (any user with editor rights — the Yorkie auth webhook only distinguishes r vs rw, packages/backend/src/document/yorkie-auth.controller.ts) produces an O(non-empty cells) read pass plus an O(styled cells) mutation pushed as one CRDT change to every peer, freezing the initiating tab and forcing all collaborators to apply it. The old `removeCellStyleKeysInRange` streamed the same scan, so this is amplification (full in-memory buffer + single mega-batch) rather than a wholly new path; `getGrid` is index-bounded, so the cost scales with stored cells, not with the 1e6-row coordinate space. No cap, chunking, or per-op budget exists on the new loop.

samples.summary: New public model-level write API `unsetRangeStyleValues` carries no read-only/permission check of its own; the only gate is the view-layer `_readOnly` flag
samples.evidence: `unsetRangeStyleValues` (sheet.ts:4238) and `changeDecimals` (sheet.ts:4195) mutate sheet, column, row, range and cell styles with no authorization or read-only check in the model. The single enforcement point is `Spreadsheet.increaseDecimals`/`decreaseDecimals` (packages/sheets/src/view/spreadsheet.ts:535, 545: `if (!this.sheet || this._readOnly) return;`). I enumerated the call sites: only packages/frontend/src/components/formatting-toolbar.tsx:249/253 reach these, both through the gated wrappers, worksheet.ts binds no decimal shortcut, and the dev-only hunt bridge (App.tsx:42 gates it behind `import.meta.env.DEV`) does not call it — so there is no bypass today, and `ReadOnlyStore` (packages/sheets/src/store/readonly.ts:81-234) no-ops the writes while the backend Yorkie auth webhook enforces r vs rw server-side. Raising it only because the new public surface is one more mutator whose enforcement lives outside it, so a future non-view caller (harness, CLI, import path) would silently write with no gate; impact today is limited to defence-in-depth.
